records.claim: The Skilled Independent visa (subclass 189), Points-tested stream, requires an Expression of Interest before invitation; the applicant must use an occupation available to the visa, provide English-test and skills-assessment information, and meet or exceed the 65-point threshold for invitation eligibility. Meeting 65 points does not guarantee an invitation.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Australian Government SkillSelect guidance; scope is restricted to subclass 189 Points-tested processing.

records.claim: The current Department of Home Affairs SkillSelect EOI guidance does not identify a separate proof-of-funds requirement in the EOI workflow. This is a scoped research finding, not a claim that the complete subclass 189 visa application has no financial obligations or fees; the route remains research_required until the visa-specific material requirements are fully verified.
records.methodology: Explicit absence check against the current official SkillSelect EOI guidance; no unsupported inference is made about the complete visa application.

records.claim: For subclass 189, an applicant submits an Expression of Interest through SkillSelect, may receive an invitation to apply, and then has 60 days from invitation to complete and submit the visa application online through ImmiAccount.
records.methodology: Direct review of the current official EOI workflow.

records.claim: Under the Skilled Migrant Category Skilled Work Experience pathway, applicants need a job or job offer from an accredited employer and must meet the pathway's skilled-work and wage conditions. Current official guidance describes a standard requirement of at least five years of directly relevant work experience, including at least two years of skilled work experience in New Zealand; age, English and other residence requirements also apply.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Immigration New Zealand SMC pathway and 2026 change guidance; exact pathway scope is preserved rather than inheriting the parent Skilled umbrella.

records.claim: Current Immigration New Zealand guidance sets the SMC wage threshold at NZD 35 per hour from 9 March 2026, with a 1.1-times median-wage threshold of NZD 38.50 for the Skilled Work Experience pathway and a 1.2-times threshold of NZD 42 for specified higher-threshold cases. The route's applicable wage threshold must be checked against the occupation and pathway conditions at decision time.
records.methodology: Direct review of the official SMC pay-rate guidance; figures are treated as effective-dated policy data, not timeless values.

records.claim: The Skilled Migrant Category uses an Expression of Interest and application process, with supporting evidence including employment agreements or job descriptions showing occupation, hours and pay and Inland Revenue earnings or tax evidence. Applicants must satisfy the route conditions at application rather than relying on the parent Skilled umbrella.
records.methodology: Direct review of official SMC application evidence guidance.

records.claim: The SMC Trades and Technician pathway requires an eligible occupation, relevant qualification and directly relevant post-qualification work experience, including at least 1.5 years of skilled work experience in New Zealand under the current pathway rules; occupation and qualification conditions must be checked against the official eligible-role and policy lists.
records.methodology: Direct review of the official 24 August 2026 SMC changes; exact occupation and qualification lists remain separate material gates.

records.claim: The current SMC Trades and Technician pathway uses the official wage thresholds: NZD 35 per hour median-wage threshold, with the pathway-specific 1.1-times threshold at NZD 38.50 and 1.2-times threshold at NZD 42 where applicable. The correct threshold depends on the occupation and pathway treatment.
records.methodology: Direct review of the official SMC pay-rate guidance.

records.claim: SMC applicants must provide evidence appropriate to the Trades and Technician pathway, including employment agreements or job descriptions and evidence of qualification and, where applicable, International Qualification Assessment treatment for overseas qualifications. The exact eligible occupation and qualification evidence must be validated before promotion.
records.methodology: Direct review of official SMC application evidence guidance.

records.claim: The Other Key Workers Red-White-Red Card route requires the prospective employer to pay at least EUR 3,465 gross per month in 2026, in addition to the route's other eligibility requirements.
records.methodology: Direct review of the official Other Key Workers route page; remuneration is treated as route-specific evidence.

records.claim: The official 2026 Flussi guidance establishes a quota-based entry system for non-seasonal subordinate work, but the reviewed source does not establish a standalone applicant proof-of-funds threshold. This is a research gap rather than evidence that no financial or employment-condition requirements apply.
records.sourceAuthority: Italian Government — Portale Integrazione Migranti / Ministry of Interior and partner ministries
records.methodology: Explicit absence check against the reviewed 2026 Flussi source; this record deliberately does not close the financial evidence gate.

records.claim: For 2026 non-seasonal subordinate work, the employer-side process uses the B2020 nulla osta application through the ALI Services Portal. The 2026 non-seasonal click day was 16 February 2026, and applications remain subject to quota availability through 31 December 2026 under the official guidance.
records.sourceAuthority: Italian Government — Portale Integrazione Migranti / Ministry of Interior and partner ministries
records.methodology: Direct review of current 2026 Flussi procedural guidance; annual click-day facts are not generalized into a timeless work-visa process.
